identityTest.stableIdentity: One actual operational-change occurrence remains identifiable independently of request, authorization, window, release, deployment, rollback and verification.
identityTest.versionIdentity: Corrections append assertion revisions under the same occurrence; retry, continuation and rollback create distinct linked execution identities.

references.purpose: Operational Change request and approved revision
Versioned window, freeze and rollback plan
Software deployment caused by this execution; association only
Verification evidence target; publication remains held

excludes: roster, assignment or IAM grant identity

PerTargetOutcome.coverageRule: covers every target in targetScope for result states

invariants: Request, authorization decision and execution have distinct identities.
Every non-emergency execution pins an approved request revision, conditions, effectivity and immutable reference digests.
Emergency execution records relaxed controls, reason, authority and retrospective due date and cannot close before retrospective authorization.
Execution begins within authorization effectivity and never after request closure.
Window and freeze constrain execution but never authorize it.
Execution inside a freeze requires a bounded authorized derogation and compensating obligation.
Rollback is a distinct execution with kind rollback and directed revertsExecutionRef.
Rollback intent, plan, execution and verified restored state remain distinct.
Restored state requires pinned verification evidence from the declared verification master.
Release, deployment and change remain separate; deployments are caused associations only.
Scheduled executions need no startedAt; terminal states require endedAt.
Partial, completed and failed executions record per-target outcomes covering targetScope.
Every instant is RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset; knowledge time orders corrections.
Execution pins the plan, window, authority and request versions it actually used; later versions never rewrite history.
Acting shift and handover intervals make the responsible party recoverable at every execution instant.
Roster membership grants no right; privileged action requires a separate time-bounded authorized grant reference or an explicit gap.
holds: WM-SFT-015 verification publication and relation contracts remain held.
Non-software target crosswalks and IAM-grant authority require canonical approval.

timePolicy.instantFormat: RFC3339 with seconds and explicit offset

lifecycleRules.terminal: completed, failed, aborted and closed require endedAt
lifecycleRules.closed: no latent or in-flight execution and no open retrospective obligation
